# missingHE: Missing Cost Effectiveness Models

> Fit Bayesian Missing Cost Effectiveness Models in R.

🚀 This is the **development version** of the `R` package `missingHE`
(currently on version 1.6.2.1). The stable version is now release 1.6.2,
on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/missingHE/index.html).

## Contents

- [Overview](#introduction)
- [Features](#features)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Further details](#further-details)

## Overview

Given a individual-level partially-observed cost-effectiveness outcome
data in the form of a dataframe, fits different types of Bayesian models
to handle missing effect and/or cost values under different assumptions
about the missing data mechanisms, assesses model performance and Markov
chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) convergence, and summarises statistical and
economic results based on the posterior distribution of key model
parameters.

## Features

Main features of `missingHE` include:

- Analysis of partially-observed effects/costs data via Bayesian
  missingness models
- Model assessment measures/plots and MCMC convergence checks
- Posterior summaries for key model parameters and cost-effectiveness
  measures
- Standard cost-effectiveness measures/graphs based on model results

## Installation

Install the [released version from
CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=missingHE) with

``` r

install.packages("missingHE")
```

The development version (in this repo, which can be updated more quickly
and more often than the stable one) can be installed using the following
command

``` r

pkgs <- c("R2jags", "ggplot2", "gridExtra", "BCEA", "ggmcmc", "loo", "Rtools", "devtools", "utils")
repos <- c("https://cran.rstudio.com") 
install.packages(pkgs, repos = repos, dependencies = "Depends")
```

before installing the package using `devtools`:

``` r

devtools::install_github("AnGabrio/missingHE", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

The optional argument `build_vignettes = TRUE` allows to install the
vignettes of the package locally on your computer. These consist in
brief tutorials to guide the user on how to use and customise the models
in `missingHE` using different functions of the package. Once the
package is installed, they can be accessed using the command

``` r

utils::browseVignettes(package = "missingHE")
```

which shows all the vignettes available for the package. Alternatively,
you can install the development version using `remotes`, with the
following command.

``` r

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("AnGabrio/missingHE")
```

**NB**: On Windows machines, you need to install a few dependencies,
including [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/)
first, e.g. by running

``` r

pkgs <- c("MASS", "Rtools", "remotes")
repos <- "https://cran.rstudio.com"
install.packages(pkgs, repos = repos, dependencies = "Depends")
```

before installing the package using `remotes`.

All models implemented in `missingHE` are written in the `BUGS` language
using the software [JAGS](https://mcmc-jags.sourceforge.io/), which
needs to be installed from its own repository and instructions for
installations under different OS can be found online. Once installed,
the software is called in `missingHE` via the `R` package
[R2jags](https://cran.r-project.org/package=R2jags). Note that the
`missingHE` package is currently under active development and therefore
it is advisable to re-install the package directly from GitHub before
each use to ensure that you are using the most updated version.

## Further details

More details on `missingHE` are available in our
[*vignettes*](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/missingHE/vignettes/).
Also, details about the package, including some references and links to
a pdf presentation and some posts on my own blog) are given
[here](https://angabrio.github.io/software/missingHE/).

# Package index

## All functions

- [`MenSS`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/MenSS.md) :
  MenSS economic data on STIs

- [`PBS`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/PBS.md) : PBS
  economic data on intellectual disability and challenging behaviour

- [`coef(`*`<missingHE>`*`)`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/coef.missingHE.md)
  :

  Extract regression coefficient estimates from objects in the class
  `missingHE`

- [`diagnostic()`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/diagnostic.md)
  :

  Diagnostic checks for assessing MCMC convergence of Bayesian models
  fitted in `JAGS` using the function `selection`, `pattern`, `hurdle`
  or `lmdm`.

- [`hurdle()`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/hurdle.md)
  : Bayesian Hurdle Models

- [`lmdm()`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/lmdm.md) :
  Bayesian Longitudinal Missing Data Models

- [`pattern()`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/pattern.md)
  : Bayesian Pattern Mixture Models

- [`pic()`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/pic.md) :

  Predictive information criteria for Bayesian models fitted in `JAGS`
  using the function `selection`, `pattern`, `hurdle` or `lmdm`

- [`plot(`*`<missingHE>`*`)`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/plot.missingHE.md)
  :

  Plot method for the imputed data contained in the objects of class
  `missingHE`

- [`postsum()`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/postsum.md)
  : Postsum method for inspecting summary posterior estimates of a
  Bayesian model fitted in JAGS

- [`ppc()`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/ppc.md) :

  Posterior predictive checks for assessing the fit to the observed data
  of Bayesian models implemented in `JAGS` using the function
  `selection`, `pattern`, `hurdle` or `lmdm`

- [`print(`*`<missingHE>`*`)`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/print.missingHE.md)
  :

  Print method for objects in the class `missingHE`

- [`selection()`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/selection.md)
  : Bayesian Selection Models

- [`summary(`*`<missingHE>`*`)`](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/reference/summary.missingHE.md)
  :

  Summary method for objects in the class `missingHE`

# Articles

### All vignettes

- [Fitting MNAR models in
  missingHE](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/articles/Fitting_MNAR_models_in_missingHE.md):

  This tutorial shows few examples of how models in missingHE can be
  fitted under different types of missing not at random (MNAR)
  assumptions for the outcome variables in trial-based CEA.

- [Introduction to
  missingHE](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/articles/Introduction_to_missingHE.md):

  Start here if this is your first time using missingHE. You will learn
  the basic theory behind the package and the most important functions
  and their arguments, which allow you to fit different types of models
  to handle missing values in trial-based CEA.

- [Longitudinal models in
  missingHE](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/articles/Longitudinal_models_in_missingHE.md):

  This tutorial shows some examples of how to specify, customise and fit
  a longitudinal missingness model in missingHE when performing
  trial-based CEA using longitudinal data.

- [Model and output customisation in
  missingHE](https://angabrio.github.io/missingHE/articles/Model_customisation_in_missingHE.md):

  This tutorial shows few examples of how different types of models and
  their output can be customised in missingHE based on the needs of the
  user when performing trial-based CEA.
